issue_context.title: Feature Request: Azure cloud shell connector
issue_context.body:
# Summary of the new feature/enhancement

<!-- 
A clear and concise description of what the problem is that the new feature would solve.
Describe why and how a user would use this new functionality (if applicable).
--> Allow Windows Terminal users to connect to the Azure cloud shell, giving them access to their Azure resources and services through Windows Terminal itself. Azure users can then much more conveniently use the Azure technologies available to them without needing to use a browser to access them. 

# Proposed technical implementation details (optional)

<!-- 
A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.
--> Authentication to Azure can be done through device code flow (at least, until Windows Terminal allows pop-up windows). Once authentication is complete, a terminal in a cloud shell instance could be requested (via HTTP) and a websocket connection can be established to the resulting URI. User commands to the cloud shell can then be sent over the websocket connection.

You're not checking if `CreateThread` actually succeeded.

If `ConhostConnection` isn't doing that either, we have two bugs.
curious why you parsed json to get the inner value, then manually created the outer value. you could manually create both, or parse json (`{"properties":{"osType":"linux"}}`) for both :smile:
Generally, define all the default values for your variables here or define them all in the constructor. But don't define some of them and not the rest.
And for the record, we've been having lots of discussions recently about how the "right" place to default initialize things is in the class definition
_initialRows and _intialCols are defined in the constructor because the constructor takes in those as arguments. I will move the initializations of the URIs to the class definition though.
All the methods should have doc comments.
doc
Added!
This sort of test will only test the first character in the string, ignoring everything after it. Is that what you want? Or do you also want to guarantee that it's a 1-length string?
Its not possible for the string to be longer than 1-length, the function is called the moment the user types anything (it does not wait for the user to press 'enter' or something)

Theoretically, all these should be in a Resources file, right? Should we file an issue + leave a note here to move them to a resources file? (I'm not going to put the evil of actually doing that on you in this PR)
Yes they are going to be moved into a resource file eventually! @DHowett said we are waiting on another PR before we move along with that
I swear the other ones above had an API version of 2019-01-01. Is this an error?
There's more below here that are 2018-01-01 too. Might be fine, it just stuck out to me.
Perhaps `"api-version=2018-01-01"` should be a constant somewhere (or whichever the correct one is)

When we send a request to _resourceUri (https://management.azure.com/) we use "api-version=2018-01-01". When we send a request to _cloudShellUri (which is a uri specific to our session), we use "version=2019-01-01" (note that it does not have "api" in front of it).
So it's intentional that they're different? It just looks like an accident/typo.
These all need to go into a resource file. Good job centralizing them, but we need to show you how to use the resource loader.
I think we might have some `DEFINE_EVENT_HANDLER` macros lying around so you don't need to put these in here manually, but they're fine for now.
Yeah. They're in src\cascadia\inc\cppwinrt_utils.h
Ah I was just following the way ConhostConnection.cpp did it
Why didn't this state get it's own helper method too?

It felt like the real meat of the output thread (since its the state we'll be in _most_ of the time) so it really was just a stylistic choice to leave it there. Can change it if anyone feels strongly about it
Consider using `std::atomic`
We need a lock guard (and a condition variable) here because we want to hold the thread until we get a valid input from the user.
